title: Orders are piling up, and some are charged twice
summary: The ledger can't always keep up, and your retries are double-charging customers.

statement.situation: Every order produces an event; the fleet emits about 6,000 events/s. A ledger service must record each one exactly once — charging a customer twice is a finance incident. The ledger can handle roughly 8,000 events/s but it occasionally stops for a short time (deploys, failovers), and the consuming side occasionally pauses and restarts for rebalancing.
symptoms: Events are lost while the ledger is down
After the ledger recovers, the backlog takes a long time to drain
Finance finds some orders recorded twice after consumer restarts
requirements: No customer may be charged twice (duplicates at the ledger ≤ 0.1%)
After a ledger outage the backlog must clear within two minutes
constraints: The ledger service is fixed — you can't change or scale it
Processing a message costs a fixed amount of time per consumer

learningObjectives: At-least-once delivery and where duplicates come from
Headroom: capacity needed to drain a backlog
Buffering versus losing work during downstream outages

references.title: Confluent: Exactly-once semantics in Apache Kafka
RabbitMQ: consumer acknowledgements and publisher confirms
Uber: reliable reprocessing and dead letter queues with Kafka
Stripe: designing robust APIs with idempotency

scenarios.name: Ledger stops for 20 s; consumers rebalance once
scenarios.description: 6,000 events/s for 5 minutes. A consumer rebalance at t=60 s; the ledger is down from t=100 s to t=120 s.

successCriteria.label: Delay back under 8 s within 2 minutes of the ledger returning
